# opencode-telegram-notify

[![CI](https://github.com/Hamza-Abili/opencode-telegram-notify/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Hamza-Abili/opencode-telegram-notify/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40hamzaabili/opencode-telegram-notify)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@hamzaabili/opencode-telegram-notify)
[![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/%40hamzaabili/opencode-telegram-notify)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@hamzaabili/opencode-telegram-notify)
[![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Hamza-Abili/opencode-telegram-notify?style=social)](https://github.com/Hamza-Abili/opencode-telegram-notify/stargazers)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](https://github.com/Hamza-Abili/opencode-telegram-notify/blob/main/LICENSE)

Telegram notifications for [OpenCode][] — **v1 and v2** — with **tap-only
inline buttons** for permission requests. Never auto-approves anything.

> 🔐 "OpenCode needs you" — permission requests, questions, completions and
> failures land in your Telegram chat while OpenCode keeps running on your
> server or workstation.

[OpenCode]: https://opencode.ai

```
🔐 Permission request
Project: my-app · Session: Fix login

shell
  > npm test

[ Allow once ] [ Reject ]
[ Always allow ]
        → tap ✅ → OpenCode continues. Nothing runs without you.
```

## Why another Telegram plugin?

Since OpenCode v2 ({id, setup} plugin contract) landed, the Telegram extensions
people know — `opencode-telegram-bot-plugin`, `opencode-channels-*`,
Tommertom's list entries — are still written against the **v1 SDK** and either
stop loading, lack permission handling, or pull a bot framework + extra shared
runtime for a task that needs none of it.

This plugin is different in four ways:

| | opencode-telegram-notify | typical alternatives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenCode versions | **v1 + v2** (two entries, one shared core) | v1 SDK only |
| Runtime dependencies | **zero** (plain `fetch`) | bot frameworks / channels stacks |
| Permissions | tap-only inline buttons → supported reply surface | missing or reply-as-prompt (hallucination risk) |
| Safety model | one bot = one chat, single-poller lock, ownership gate, event dedupe | assumptions |

Scope is deliberate: **notifications + tap-only permission buttons**. It is not
a chat-with-your-agent relay, it never injects text into your sessions.

## Features

- 🔌 **Works with OpenCode v1 and v2** — the v2 default export (`{id, setup}`)
  and a v1 `legacy` entry share the same core; only events transport and
  permission reply surface differ per version.
- 🔐 **Permission requests** as messages with three buttons: *Allow once*,
  *Always allow*, *Reject* — mapped to `client.permission.reply`
  (`once` / `always` / `reject`). Tap-only: no free text, no prompt injection,
  no auto-approval.
- ✍️ **Live feedback** — buttons are replaced with ✅/🚫 confirmations and a
  toast appears on tap; on next OpenCode restart older buttons answer politely
  with "outdated" instead of dying silently.
- ❓ **Questions** (v2 `form.*`) answered in chat: questions with one choice
  field (2–5 options) arrive as tap buttons (answer via `session.form.reply`
  when available, otherwise `question.reply`; skip via `session.form.cancel`
  when available, otherwise `question.reject`). String fields send the selected
  value and multiselect fields send a one-item array. Other question types stay
  notify-only with the terminal pointer, and pending questions survive restarts
  (`question.list` recovery). When the host exposes no reply surface (the
  current OpenCode v2 plugin context through 2.2.5 exposes none for forms —
  tracked upstream in
  [anomalyco/opencode#51108](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/51108)),
  the message is notify-only with the terminal pointer instead of showing dead
  buttons.
- ✅ / ❌ / ⏹ **Lifecycle events** — completion (debounced so mid-run pauses
  don't spam), failure with error type, cancellation (silent). Completion
  messages include the session's cumulative **token and cost usage** when the
  host reports it (OpenCode v2; `⚡ 13.2k in · 3.2k out · $0.042`). Failures
  caused by a **usage limit** (OpenCode free tier, provider quota, rate
  limits; Console budgets on hosts that emit them) get a friendly headline
  instead of the raw error code, e.g. `⛔ Free usage limit reached`.
- 🤖 **Bot command menu** — `/start`, `/status`, `/setup`, `/stop`, `/help`
  registered via `setMyCommands`, so the ☰ menu works out of the box.
  `/setup` prints a copy-paste-ready `opencode.jsonc` block.
- 🏠 **Multi-instance safe** — several OpenCode instances on one host: each
  notifies only for its own project root; a single-poller file lock guarantees
  only one process consumes `getUpdates`; process-level event-id dedupe means
  reloads don't double-send.
- 🌐 **en / it** notification language.
- 🔒 **Private by default** — `hideCommands: true` replaces shell/tool args with
  a count; every log line and error message is token-redacted.

## Requirements

- OpenCode **v2** (tested on 2.2.5; the 2.0.x line is also supported) or **v1.18+**
  (the hooks-based `@opencode-ai/plugin` contract, e.g. the 1.18/1.19 line).
  v1 has no per-plugin options, so its configuration is environment-driven only.
- A Telegram bot token (via [@BotFather] — takes one minute) and the chat id of
  your user or group.
- [Bun] **only if you run the dev tooling** (typecheck/tests). The plugin itself
  runs inside OpenCode with zero extra installs.

[@BotFather]: https://t.me/BotFather
[Bun]: https://bun.sh

## Install (3 minutes)

### 1. Create the bot and get your chat id

1. In Telegram, chat with `@BotFather`, send `/newbot`, follow prompts, copy the
   token (looks like `123456789:AA…`).
2. Send `/start` to your bot once, then find your numeric chat id — the
   `/start` reply echoes your chat id in a copy block, or message
   `@userinfobot`.

### 2. Point OpenCode at the plugin

**OpenCode v2** — add it to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`. Use a source
checkout path (works on every v2 build) or the npm name where supported:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "/absolute/path/to/opencode-telegram-notify",
      "options": {
        "telegram": {
          "botToken": "${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}",
          "chatId": "${TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID}"
        },
        "language": "en"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

(the npm form `"package": "@hamzaabili/opencode-telegram-notify"` is verified:
the v2 loader resolves the name from the registry and caches it under
`~/.cache/opencode/npm/`; other builds may only accept absolute paths.)

**OpenCode v1** — register the `legacy` entry as a plugin name in
`opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "plugin": [
    "@hamzaabili/opencode-telegram-notify/legacy"
  ]
}
```

If your v1 build does not resolve npm package specifiers, clone this repo and
point the entry at the local file:

```json
{ "plugin": ["/absolute/path/to/opencode-telegram-notify/src/legacy.ts"] }
```

### 3. Provide the environment

The plugin expands `${VAR}` in option values and falls back to the flat env
names, so secrets never sit in `opencode.jsonc`:

```sh
export TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN="123456789:AA…"
export TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID="123456789"        # negative number for group chats
export TELEGRAM_LANGUAGE="en"              # optional (mainly for OpenCode v1)
```

(For a `systemd` unit or `docker compose` install, pass these environment
variables into the OpenCode process environment.)

### 4. Restart OpenCode

- if `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` was unset, run `/start` in the bot chat — the reply
  already contains your chat id inside a `<code>` block;
- every future permission request arrives as a message you can answer by tap.

## Configuration reference

All options live under `options.` of the plugin entry. Only `botToken` and
`chatId` are required.

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `telegram.botToken` | string | — | Bot token; `"${VAR}"` expands from process env |
| `telegram.chatId` | string | — | Destination chat (user id or negative group id) |
| `telegram.allowedUserIds` | string[] | `[]` | Extra guard: only these Telegram user ids may tap buttons or run commands (empty = everyone reaching this bot token) |
| `language` | `"en" \| "it"` | `"en"` | Notification language |
| `events.permission` | boolean | `true` | Permission request notifications + buttons |
| `events.question` | boolean | `true` | Question (`form.created`) notifications |
| `events.idle` | boolean | `true` | Completion notifications (debounced) |
| `events.error` | boolean | `true` | Failure and cancellation notifications (limit refusals included, with a friendly label) |
| `events.usage` | boolean | `true` | Token and cost line on completion notifications (v2 only; v1 hosts report no usage and the line is omitted) |
| `interactions` | boolean | `true` | When `false`, permissions go out as simple messages (no buttons) |
| `idleDebounceMs` | number | 60000 | Wait after `execution.succeeded` before pinging you; any new activity cancels it |
| `idleCooldownMs` | number | 600000 | Min gap between completion notifications for the same session — conversational pauses never spam (0 disables) |
| `maxMessageChars` | number | 3800 | Max body length (Telegram hard limit is 4096) |
| `hideCommands` | boolean | `false` | Replace shell/tool arguments with `[n]` in bodies |
| `logFile` | string | off | Append-only debug log path (token-redacted, one line per event) |

## Commands

Registered on the bot menu (☰); unknown commands and plain messages are
ignored — this is a notifier, not a chat relay.

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `/start` | Re-enables a silenced chat; echoes your chat id in a copy-block |
| `/status` | Running state, project root, which event groups are on |
| `/setup` | Copy-paste-ready `opencode.jsonc` snippet (with placeholders, never your token) |
| `/stop` | Silence notifications in this chat until `/start` |
| `/help` | Short command list |

## How it fits OpenCode

- v2 plugin entry is the `{id, setup}` contract — `setup` subscribes to the
  event stream, starts the poller, and returns a dispose.
- v1 entry (`./legacy`) is a hooks factory: bus events arrive through the
  `event` hook and permission answers go over the v1 SDK surface
  `POST /session/{id}/permissions/{permissionID}` with body `{ response }`
  (or the modern `permission.reply` client namespace when present). Both v1
  permission generations are accepted on the event side:
  `permission.updated {id, title, metadata}` (pre-rework hosts) and
  `permission.asked {id, permission, patterns, metadata, always, tool?}`
  (post-rework v1.x). On v1, `MessageAbortedError` maps to the *silent*
  interruption notification (a user abort is not a failure); v1 has no
  `form.*` flow, so questions are simply not available there. Note: the bot's
  `/setup` reply always prints the v2 `plugins[]` config shape; on v1 copy the
  `plugin: [...]` entry from this README instead.
- Events used: `permission.asked/replied`, `form.created/replied/cancelled`,
  `session.execution.succeeded/failed/interrupted`, plus `session.created`,
  `session.renamed` and activity events for the debounce/ownership logic.
- Permission answers go through the supported surface
  `client.permission.reply({ sessionID, requestID, decision })`; a legacy
  `reply`-key shape is attempted (and logged) if the server rejects `decision`.
- Only events whose `location.directory` resolves to this OpenCode root are
  handled — a conversation in another project never triggers your bot.

## Multi-instance behavior

One host can run several OpenCode instances (different roots, same bot token):

- the first instance that wins the cache-dir file lock (`~/.cache/
  opencode-telegram-notify/poller.lock`, with liveness heartbeat) consumes
  Telegram updates and serves the chat;
- every instance is notified only about its own root, so taps are routed by
  whichever instance is polling;
- losing activation (crash, machine restart), staleness after ~30 s lets the
  next instance take over.

## Troubleshooting

- **409 Conflict in the log** — another process (old activation or another app)
  is polling the same token; the poller backs off automatically. Check you did
  not reuse a token in `opencode-telegram-monitor` or another bot.
- **Nothing arrives** — verify the two env vars are visible *to the OpenCode
  process*, and that `options.telegram.botToken` is not a literal placeholder.
  Set `logFile` to a path and watch it while you drive OpenCode.
- **Buttons say "outdated"** — the message predates the current activation
  (buttons are routed through this instance's pending map). Answer in the
  terminal as usual.
- **Config error** — misconfiguration never crashes OpenCode: you get a clear
  `configuration error: …` line (stderr/`logFile`) and the plugin disables
  itself for that session.

## Deferred ideas

Deliberately not scheduled; revisit when they earn their complexity:

- menu-style settings keyboard (runtime config writes are outside the
  current plugin surface);
- reply-to-message → in-session notes (extra control channel);
- multi-field question wizards (open, keep notify-only for now).

## Other OpenCode plugins by the same author

Same constraints: MIT, zero runtime dependencies, OpenCode V1 + V2.

- [opencode-agent-plugins](https://github.com/Hamza-Abili/opencode-agent-plugins) — Agent Plugins 1.0 client: discovery from `.agents/plugins` and npm packages, native skills, trust-first MCP registration.
- [opencode-sandbox](https://github.com/Hamza-Abili/opencode-sandbox) — native command sandbox: bubblewrap on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS, fail-closed, network denied by default.

# Changelog

## 0.5.2 — packaging and discoverability only

- No runtime changes: `src/` and `index.ts` are identical to 0.5.1.
- Added `homepage` and the `telegram-bot` keyword to `package.json`, and a
  short cross-link section for the other plugins by the same author.

## 0.5.1 — question answers match the form schema

- `session.form.reply` now sends a string for `string` fields and a one-item
  array for `multiselect` fields. The old array-only shape was rejected by
  `Form.validateAnswer` for the built-in `question` tool's single-select
  fields, so taps would have failed as soon as a host exposed the form reply
  surface.
- Skip prefers `session.form.cancel` when the host exposes it, falling back
  to `question.reject` on older hosts; the skip button is offered when either
  surface exists.
- Tests cover both answer shapes and both skip surfaces (130 tests). On
  OpenCode 2.1.x the plugin context still exposes no form surface, so
  questions remain notify-only until upstream
  [#51108](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/51108) lands.

## 0.5.0 — token usage on completions and limit labels

- Completion notifications now append the session's cumulative usage line
  (`⚡ 13.2k in · 3.2k out · $0.042`) read through the supported
  `session.get` surface — no HTTP port sniffing, no per-event accounting.
  Folded into the existing single completion lookup (which already fetched
  the title); `events.usage: false` disables the line. v1 hosts simply omit
  it. Prompt side folds in cache read+write, response side reasoning (same
  grouping upstream bills); the cost segment is dropped when it rounds to
  zero.
- Failure notifications caused by a usage limit (`provider.free-limit`,
  `provider.quota`, `provider.rate-limit`, `provider.budget-limit`,
  `provider.model-budget-limit`) show a friendly en/it headline instead of
  the raw error code; the upstream message is kept underneath.
- New tests cover the usage line, its omission when the host reports
  nothing, the `events.usage` flag, the formatting helpers, and the limit
  labels (127 tests). The two Console-budget labels are forward-looking:
  v2.1.4 core emits the free-tier/quota/rate-limit types; budget types land
  when the Console budget flow reaches core.

## 0.4.4 — discoverability and upstream version watch

- npm keywords expanded for search/discovery, and the package now declares its
  OpenDock-detectable compatibility explicitly: `engines.opencode`
  (`>=1.18 <2 || >=2.0`) plus the `opencode-v1` / `opencode-v2` keywords
  (the plugin has zero runtime deps, so the SDK-dependency signal OpenDock
  usually uses is absent by design). GitHub topics extended too.
- New `upstream-watch` workflow (weekly + manual): opens a "Review
  compatibility with OpenCode <version>" issue when a new upstream release
  lands, with the release notes and the compatibility checklist, instead of
  letting the plugin drift silently. It reads upstream **tags** (OpenCode
  publishes GitHub Releases only for the v1 line; v2 ships as tags + npm),
  and skips with a warning if the README version anchor is missing.
- README: tested on OpenCode 2.1.4; v1 floor documented as 1.18+; the
  question-button fallback now links the upstream tracking issue
  ([anomalyco/opencode#51108](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/51108)).

## 0.4.3 — question surface guard and safer taps

- Question buttons are attached only when the client actually exposes a reply
  surface; otherwise the form is notify-only with the terminal pointer
  (OpenCode 2.1.1 currently exposes none, so questions there are notify-only).
- Permission and question taps share one best-effort outcome helper. Failed
  replies keep the message **and its buttons** for a retry (toast only), while
  a failed confirmation edit can no longer turn a successful reply into a
  misleading "tap again" error.
- Question skip is offered only when a reject surface exists, prefers the
  global surface and falls back to the scoped one when the global cannot
  reject, and `session.form.reply` errors are preserved when there is no
  fallback so settled requests are still recognized.
- Completion notifications show project + cached session title once (no
  duplicated title); every message header now carries the project name.
- Bot command registration is attempted once per ownership acquisition (and
  retried after a lost/regained lock) instead of every poll cycle, so a failing
  `setMyCommands` cannot hammer the API.
- CI runs Biome lint and installs with `--frozen-lockfile` (release too).
- README: tested on OpenCode 2.1.1; stale `dedupTtlMs` row removed;
  `session.form.cancel` noted as a future skip surface.

## 0.4.2

- Version bump to refresh the OpenCode npm cache; contains the 0.4.1 reply
  diagnostics.

## 0.4.1

- `logReplyError()` records code/status/message/cause/response (token-redacted)
  to diagnose false "already answered" reports.

## 0.4.0 — reliability, safety and ergonomics

- **Event stream cancellation**: proper `AbortSignal` integration with
  `subscribe({ signal })`, positional fallback, and iterator `return()` on
  dispose — works on official 2.0.32 and is forward-compatible.
- **Poller lock hardening**: per-activation token in the lock file prevents
  same-process double-release; atomic heartbeat via tmp+rename; stale-lock
  recovery now tolerates torn writes without deadlocking.
- **Permission reply shape caching**: first successful `decision`/`reply`
  key is remembered per activation, eliminating repeated fallback probes.
- **Pending reply semantics**: transient failures (network, 5xx) keep the
  button active for retry; settled errors (404/409, "already answered") close
  the message with "already answered" toast.
- **Multi-instance honesty**: only the poller lock owner attaches interactive
  buttons; standby instances send notify-only messages with a terminal hint.
  `/status` shows interactive/standby state.
- **Session cleanup**: `session.deleted` events clear titles, attribution
  indexes and pending button state; all caches bounded (500 entries) to
  prevent unbounded growth on long-running hosts.
- **HTML-safe truncation**: `truncateHtml()` never cuts tags/entities and
  closes open tags when `maxMessageChars` forces a cut.
- **Config fixes**: `allowedUserIds` expansion drops empty entries; numeric
  parsing rejects partial strings (`"15s"` → fallback); `dedupTtlMs` removed.
- **i18n polish**: per-session cooldown never spams; new strings for
  `PERMISSION_ANSWER_IN_TERMINAL`, `REPLY_FAILED_RETRY`, `/status` labels,
  command descriptions; Italian translations updated.
- **Test isolation**: poller tests use unique temp dirs (`mkdtempSync`) and
  fast timers (`longPollSeconds: 0`, `pollIntervalMs: 5`), eliminating
  flakiness from shared state.
- **Code quality**: Biome lint/format added (`biome.json`, `lint`, `format`
  scripts); dead code removed (`formatError`, `listPermissions`, `TITLE`,
  `dedupTtlMs`, `TelegramError` re-export); types aligned with official
  `@opencode/plugin@2.0.32` surfaces.

## 0.3.1 — no more completion spam

- **Per-session completion cooldown** (`idleCooldownMs`, default 10 min):
  an interactive session pauses often, but Telegram now receives at most one
  "✅ Task completed" per session per cooldown window. Permission, question,
  failure and cancellation notifications are never delayed.
- **Details always meaningful**: the title is resolved at send time — cache,
  then `session.get` write-through — and falls back to the project name, so
  "(no details)" no longer appears on completions for sessions that started
  before the plugin activation.
- **Calmer default debounce**: `idleDebounceMs` default 15 s → 60 s.

## 0.3.0 — in-chat question answering (wizard)

- **Answer questions from Telegram**: single-select questions (`form.created`
  with one option field) now arrive as inline tap buttons; one tap sends
  `question.reply` (global surface first, session-scoped
  `session.question.reply` fallback, logged). Tap-only still: nothing is ever
  auto-submitted.
- **⏹ Skip button** on questions uses `question.reject`.
- **Restart recovery**: pending questions are re-listed on activation
  (`question.list`) and re-rendered with buttons; a later `form.created` for
  the same form id no longer duplicates the message.
- Multi-field and free-form questions remain notify-only with the terminal
  pointer (documented in README "Deferred ideas").
- Dependabot: npm ecosystem removed (Bun-managed lockfile kept failing weekly
  updates); GitHub Actions ecosystem stays.
- Release workflow: npm publish idempotence guard is now name-agnostic
  (`npm pkg get name`) with a staging-window comment.

## 0.2.2 — poller offset persistence and redelivery fixes

- Offset now persisted to `poller.offset.json` alongside the lock file; survives
  process restarts and prevents reprocessing old updates on plugin reload.
- Process-level dedupe set (`Symbol.for("opencode-telegram-notify/seen-updates")`)
  ignores already-seen `update_id` values within the same process lifetime.
- Offset is advanced **only after** successful `dispatch()` and persisted
  immediately; on `getUpdates` failure (non-409) the offset is not advanced and
  the same offset is retried next cycle.
- New test coverage: offset persistence across restarts, in-process dedupe on
  redelivery, and proper offset advancement ordering.

## 0.2.1 — (internal) offset advancement fix

## 0.2.0 — dual v1/v2 support and npm distribution

- One package, two entry points sharing the same core:
  - `.` — OpenCode v2 default export `{id, setup}` (unchanged);
  - `./legacy` — OpenCode v1 hooks factory, usable as
    `@hamzaabili/opencode-telegram-notify/legacy` in the v1 `"plugin"` config.
- v1 event mapping: `permission.updated` (pre-rework:
  `{id, sessionID, title, metadata}`) and `permission.asked` (post-rework
  v1.x: `{id, sessionID, permission, patterns, metadata, always, tool?}`)
  both map to the shared asked-envelope; `permission.replied` accepts both
  `{permissionID, response}` and `{requestID, reply}` field generations;
  `session.created/updated/deleted` with a title ledger that only forwards
  real changes; `session.status` → activity; `session.idle` → completion;
  `session.error` → failure, with `MessageAbortedError` mapped to the
  *silent* interruption notice.
- Permissions on v1 are answered through the legacy surface
  `POST /session/{id}/permissions/{permissionID}` body `{ response }`, with
  an automatic fallback to the modern `permission.reply({requestID, reply})`
  client namespace when the host exposes it (the fallback is logged).
- `TELEGRAM_LANGUAGE` environment fallback (v1 has no per-plugin options);
  explicit options keep precedence.
- Poller heartbeat and idle timers are unref'ed so the plugin can never keep
  a server process alive on v1 hosts, which expose no dispose chain.
- npm distribution as the scoped package `@hamzaabili/opencode-telegram-notify`
  (the unscoped name is occupied by an unrelated project) and free CI/CD:
  `release.yml` (tag → typecheck/tests → GitHub Release → optional
  `NPM_TOKEN`-based npm publish) plus Dependabot.
- v1 host test hooks: mapper (both permission generations), client shim
  (legacy + modern surfaces incl. fallback), bounded queue, and disabled-path
  factory tested — 72 tests across 7 files.

## 0.1.0 — first public release

- v2-native plugin contract: `export default { id, setup }`, zero runtime
  dependencies (plain `fetch`).
- Permission notifications with tap-only inline buttons (*Allow once* /
  *Always allow* / *Reject*) through `client.permission.reply`
  (`decision`, with logged fallback to the legacy `reply` key shape).
- Question (`form.created`) notify-only messages with fields and options;
  auto-close on `form.replied` / `form.cancelled` ("answered"/"cancelled").
- Lifecycle notifications: completion (debounced by activity),
  failure with error type/message, silent cancellation.
- Chat bindings and allowlists: `telegram.chatId`, optional
  `telegram.allowedUserIds`; unknown chats ignored.
- Bot command menu via `setMyCommands`: `/start`, `/status`, `/setup`,
  `/stop`, `/help`; unknown commands get help, plain text ignored.
- `/setup` reply with copy-paste `opencode.jsonc` snippet and env hints.
- Safety: single-poller file lock (pid + heartbeat), ownership gate on
  `location.directory`, process-level event-id dedupe (Symbol.for set, capped),
  subagent sessions excluded from lifecycle noise, stale-button toasts.
- Privacy: `hideCommands` option, token redaction in errors/`logFile`,
  `${VAR}`-based secrets, optional append-only `logFile`.
- i18n: English and Italian.
- Test suite (bun): config, formatting, router, callbacks, lock, telegram
  client — `bun run ci`.
